open_questions: Which sector represents the true unblended depth — the 7412 ppm shallow sector or the 15699 ppm deep sector?
Is depth scatter due to changing contamination/detector systematics or a few bad transits (top-3 carry 1.0)?
Centroid is inconclusive; high-resolution imaging/ground-based on-target transits needed at predicted depth
dossier.public_summary: TESS shows only three short dips (about 1.7 hr, 13.7 days, 1.2%) that are flat-bottomed but not equally deep: one sector is about half as deep as another and the single transit depths disagree. A planet on the target can look flat but not change this much, and we have no centroid image to prove the dip is on the target. The best explanation is either a planet seen through variable contamination with no confirmed depth, or a background blended eclipsing binary, so the signal is rejected as a confirmed planet.

reasons.why: Depth more than doubles between sectors with very high chi2 (15.44/1); alone this is expected from apertures, but with only two sectors it leaves two competing explanations with no timeseries to break degeneracy.
Change is within one source (QLP) not between products, so not a calibration difference; true depth variation as observed.
